source_document: Marghoob AA, Usatine RP, Jaimes N. Dermoscopy for the Family Physician. Am Fam Physician. 2013;88(7):441-450, including Online Appendix pp A-F.

triples.subject: pigment_network
triples.notes: Melanocytic lesion resolves to nv or mel at step 2; no single DermaMNIST label. Histopathologic correlate: melanin in keratinocytes or melanocytes along the dermoepidermal junction; network lines correspond to the rete ridges; holes correspond to the suprapapillary plate.

triples.subject: negative_pigment_network
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: remains unknown; presumed related to bridging of rete ridges or large melanocytic nests in the papillary dermis.

triples.subject: aggregated_globules
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: nests of melanocytes at the dermoepidermal junction.

triples.subject: streaks
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: confluent junctional nests of melanocytes.

triples.subject: pseudopods
triples.source: Table 4, level 1, p444; Appendix, Melanocytic Neoplasms, p A

triples.subject: radial_streaming
triples.source: Table 4, level 1, p444; Appendix, Melanocytic Neoplasms, p A

triples.subject: pseudonetwork
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: pigment in the epidermis or dermis in which the rete ridges are attenuated.

triples.subject: pseudonetwork

triples.notes: Table 4 says '(facial skin)'; appendix says 'usually seen in facial lesions'.

triples.subject: parallel_pigment_pattern
triples.source: Table 4, level 1, p444; Appendix p B
triples.notes: Acral lesions on palms and soles.

triples.subject: dermatofibroma
triples.notes: Dermatofibroma is nonmelanocytic yet displays pigment network, a level 1 melanocytic criterion. Palpation/dimpling clue deliberately excluded as it is not an image feature.

triples.subject: peripheral_delicate_pigment_network
triples.notes: Only positive dermatofibroma evidence in the entire document.

triples.subject: dermatofibroma
triples.verbatim: Dermatofibromas are characterized by a peripheral delicate pigment network with a central scar-like area.

triples.subject: dermatofibroma
triples.notes: Confusion arises specifically at the step-1 melanocytic/nonmelanocytic boundary via the pigment network.

triples.subject: arborizing_vessels
triples.source: Table 4, level 2, p444; Appendix, Vascular Structures in Nonmelanocytic Tumors, p D; p444 col 1
triples.notes: Appendix NOTE: can also, on rare occasions, be seen in melanoma and intradermal nevi; also seen in cysts, furuncles and other adnexal tumors. Body text p444 col 1: nonpigmented BCC can reveal arborizing blood vessels.

triples.subject: leaf_like_structures
triples.source: Table 4, level 2, p444; Appendix p C
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: large pigmented basal cell carcinoma tumor nests in the upper dermis. Body text p444 col 1 lists this among pigmented BCC structures.

triples.subject: large_blue_gray_ovoid_nests

triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: large basal cell carcinoma tumor nests in the dermis.

triples.subject: blue_gray_globules_or_dots

triples.subject: blue_gray_globules_or_dots

triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: small basal cell carcinoma tumor nests in the dermis.

triples.subject: blue_gray_globules_or_dots
triples.notes: Nonaggregated distribution separates these from level 1 aggregated globules; the source states the aggregation contrast implicitly through the two criterion wordings.

triples.subject: spoke_wheel_structures
triples.source: Table 4, level 2, p444; Appendix p C
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: basal cell carcinoma tumor nests radiating from the dermoepidermal junction.

triples.subject: concentric_structures
triples.source: Table 4, level 2, p444; Figure 4 caption, p448

triples.subject: white_shiny_structures
triples.verbatim: Additional features for basal cell carcinoma include white shiny structures (i.e., white shiny areas and white shiny streaks, also known as crystalline structures)

triples.subject: white_shiny_areas
triples.source: Table 4 footnote †, p444; Appendix p B

triples.subject: crystalline_structures
triples.source: Table 4 footnote †, p444; Appendix p B

triples.subject: ulceration

triples.subject: milia_like_cysts

triples.subject: milia_like_cysts

triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: intraepidermal keratin-filled cysts.

triples.subject: comedo_like_openings
triples.source: Table 4, level 3, p444; Figure 5 caption, p448
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: concave invaginations in the surface of the epidermis filled with keratin; some may correspond to follicular openings filled with keratin.

triples.subject: moth_eaten_borders

triples.subject: gyri_and_sulci

triples.subject: fingerprint_like_structures
triples.source: Table 4, level 3, p444; Appendix p C
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: epidermal ridges.

triples.subject: sharp_demarcation

triples.notes: Clinical rather than dermoscopic description in the source.

triples.subject: seborrheic_keratosis
triples.verbatim: They range from light brown to dark brown or black.

triples.subject: lacunae

triples.subject: black_lacunae

triples.subject: cherry_hemangioma
triples.verbatim: Cherry hemangiomas are bright red to violaceous papules that consist of dilated capillaries.

triples.subject: angiokeratoma
triples.verbatim: angiokeratomas are dark violaceous to black papules that are often keratotic or firm on palpation
triples.notes: Palpation component is not an image feature.

triples.subject: lacunae
triples.notes: Discrimination is by lacuna color, not by lacuna presence: red is hemangioma-only, black is angiokeratoma-only, maroon is shared.

triples.subject: lacunae
triples.verbatim: lagoons often separated by septae

triples.verbatim: No structures or blood vessels noted

triples.subject: streaks
triples.notes: Table 5 qualifies streaks as focally and asymmetrically distributed; undifferentiated streaks are a level 1 melanocytic criterion.

triples.subject: regression_structures
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: scar-like changes/white areas correspond to thickened fibrotic papillary dermis; blue areas correlate with melanosis type of regression.

triples.subject: regression_structures
triples.verbatim: combination of scar-like depigmentation and peppering gives the appearance of a blue-white veil

triples.subject: blue_white_veil
triples.notes: Table 5 entry is 'Blue-white veil overlying raised areas'.

triples.subject: blue_white_veil
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: aggregation of heavily pigmented melanocytes or melanophages combined with compact orthokeratosis of the stratum corneum.

triples.subject: crystalline_structures
triples.notes: Direct conflict with t_039: crystalline structures are also listed as an additional BCC feature in Table 4 footnote †.

triples.subject: peripheral_brown_structureless_areas
triples.verbatim: Tan areas located at the periphery of the lesion that encompass greater than 10% of the lesion

triples.subject: melanoma_specific_structures
triples.verbatim: Any of the melanoma-specific structures can also be seen in Spitz nevi.
triples.notes: Applies to all ten structures individually; the single most important false-positive route toward mel in this graph.

triples.subject: melanoma
triples.notes: Melanomas reveal at least one of the 10 melanoma-specific structures (p443 col 2).

triples.subject: melanocytic_nevus

triples.notes: Root node of the algorithm topology.

triples.subject: two_step_algorithm_step_2
triples.notes: Step 2 applies only to the melanocytic branch of step 1; its three terminal verdicts are nevus, suspect and malignant.

triples.subject: basal_cell_carcinoma
triples.verbatim: occasionally basal cell carcinoma and melanoma can manifest overlapping features that may lead to the incorrect classification of some basal cell carcinomas as melanocytic (i.e., melanoma) and some melanomas as nonmelanocytic (i.e., basal cell carcinoma)
triples.notes: Bidirectional at the step-1 melanocytic/nonmelanocytic boundary; see t_170 for the reverse direction.

triples.subject: melanoma

triples.subject: pigment_network

triples.subject: aggregated_globules
triples.verbatim: Diameters are greater than 0.1 mm

triples.subject: aggregated_globules
triples.verbatim: More than three clustered, well-demarcated, round to oval, symmetric structures, or three or more of these structures aligned at the lesion's perimeter

triples.subject: aggregated_globules
triples.verbatim: May be brown, black, or blue

triples.subject: dots
triples.verbatim: Small, round structures of less than 0.1 mm in diameter
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: aggregates of melanocytes or melanin granules.

triples.subject: dots
triples.verbatim: May be black, brown, or blue-gray

triples.subject: dots
triples.notes: The 0.1 mm diameter threshold is the sole discriminator between dots and globules in this source.

triples.subject: pseudopods
triples.verbatim: Pseudopods are streaks with finger-like projections with small knobs at the tips

triples.subject: radial_streaming
triples.verbatim: Radial streaming is streaks without knobs at the tips

triples.subject: pseudopods
triples.notes: Presence or absence of terminal knobs is the discriminator.

triples.subject: peppering
triples.verbatim: Tiny, blue-gray granules
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: melanin deposited as intracellular (mostly within melanophages) or extracellular particles in the upper dermis. Also called granularity.

triples.subject: structureless_areas
triples.verbatim: Devoid of dermoscopic structures within the lesion and without manifesting any regression structures
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: relative decreased concentration of melanin or flattening of rete ridges.

triples.subject: peripheral_brown_structureless_areas
triples.verbatim: Structureless areas (as above), located at the periphery of the lesion

triples.subject: peripheral_brown_structureless_areas
triples.verbatim: encompass greater than 10% of the lesion
triples.notes: The >10% threshold appears only in Table 5; the appendix entry omits it. Histopathologic correlate: partial or complete flattening of the rete ridges; increased number of pigmented atypical melanocytes predominantly at the dermoepidermal junction; diffuse scattering of melanocytes in the spinous layer of the epidermis.

triples.subject: blotches
triples.verbatim: Dark brown to black homogeneous areas of pigment that obscure visualization of any other structures
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: aggregates of melanin in the stratum corneum or throughout all layers of the skin.

triples.subject: scar_like_depigmentation
triples.verbatim: lighter than the surrounding uninvolved normal skin; appear shiny white under polarized dermoscopy

triples.subject: blue_white_veil
triples.verbatim: Confluent blue pigmentation with an overlying white ground-glass haze

triples.subject: rosettes
triples.verbatim: appear as four white shiny points creating a pattern reminiscent of a four-leaf clover
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlation has not been fully explained.

triples.subject: crystalline_structures
triples.verbatim: short, white, shiny linear streaks that are often parallel or orthogonal to each other
triples.notes: Table 5 wording differs slightly: 'White shiny streaks or lines organized orthogonally'. Histopathologic correlate: altered collagen or fibrosis in the dermis.

triples.subject: white_shiny_areas
triples.verbatim: appear as larger structureless areas of shiny white color
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: altered stromal matrix.

triples.subject: parallel_pigment_pattern
triples.verbatim: Parallel rows of pigmentation following the furrows (as seen in nevi) or ridges (as seen in melanoma) of the dermatoglyphics

triples.subject: parallel_furrow_pattern
triples.verbatim: furrows (as seen in nevi)
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: pigmented melanocytes in the furrows (crista limitants) on skin of palms and soles.

triples.subject: parallel_ridge_pattern
triples.verbatim: ridges (as seen in melanoma)
triples.notes: Histopathologic correlate: pigmented melanocytes in the ridges (crista intermedia) on skin of palms and soles.

triples.subject: parallel_pigment_pattern
triples.notes: Polarity: furrow localization is benign, ridge localization is malignant. Same parent structure, opposite classes.

triples.subject: white_shiny_structures
triples.verbatim: more conspicuous with polarized dermoscopy
triples.notes: Kept because it qualifies the definition; imaging modality is not recoverable from a HAM10000 label, so this should not be used as reasoning evidence.

triples.subject: milia_like_cysts
triples.verbatim: Round whitish or yellowish structures that shine brightly (like "stars in the sky") under nonpolarized dermoscopy

triples.subject: comedo_like_openings
triples.verbatim: Blackhead-like plugs on the surface of the lesion

triples.subject: fingerprint_like_structures
triples.verbatim: Delicate, thin, light brown parallel running lines that do not interconnect to form a grid

triples.subject: fingerprint_like_structures
triples.notes: Failure to interconnect into a grid is what separates these from a pigment network.

triples.subject: gyri_and_sulci
triples.verbatim: Gyri (ridges or fat fingers) and sulci (fissures) that create a cerebriform surface

triples.subject: moth_eaten_borders
triples.verbatim: Concave invaginations of the lesion border

triples.subject: pigment_network_like_structure

triples.subject: pigment_network_like_structure

triples.subject: leaf_like_structures

triples.subject: spoke_wheel_structures

triples.subject: spoke_wheel_structures

triples.subject: large_blue_gray_ovoid_nests
triples.verbatim: Large, well-circumscribed ovoid areas; larger than globules

triples.subject: blue_gray_globules_or_dots

triples.subject: blue_gray_globules_or_dots

triples.subject: crown_vessels
triples.notes: Mimic node; no DermaMNIST class.

triples.subject: crown_vessels

criteria.name: three_point_checklist

components.verbatim: Asymmetry in distribution of dermoscopic color and/or structures in one or two perpendicular axes.
Irregular or atypical pigment network consisting of thick lines and irregular holes.
Blue-white veil and/or white scar-like depigmentation and/or blue pepper-like granules.

criteria.known_limitation: Figure 8 lesions C and D each scored 2 and were diagnosed as basal cell carcinoma, not melanoma. A positive score therefore does not discriminate mel from bcc. Lesion C additionally had a clinically symmetric oval contour while being dermoscopically asymmetric.
criteria.verbatim: A total score of 2 or 3 is considered positive

criteria.name: pattern_analysis_melanoma_conjunction

components.notes: Deviation from one of the nine Figure 3 benign patterns.
At least one of the ten Table 5 structures.

criteria.known_limitation: Table 5 footnote: any of the melanoma-specific structures can also be seen in Spitz nevi, so the conjunction can fire on a Spitz nevus.
criteria.verbatim: Any melanocytic lesion that deviates from one of these benign patterns, while also revealing at least one of the 10 melanoma-specific structures, should be biopsied to rule out melanoma.

criteria.name: melanoma_specific_structure_presence
criteria.known_limitation: Table 5 footnote: any of these structures can also be seen in Spitz nevi.
criteria.verbatim: melanomas reveal at least one of the 10 melanoma-specific structures provided in Table 5

criteria.name: vascular_evidence_weighting_rule

components.notes: Vessel morphology and distribution are the only diagnostic clue.
Vascular structures provide secondary clues only.

criteria.verbatim: In most amelanotic and hypomelanotic lesions, the only clue to the diagnosis depends on evaluating the blood vessel morphology and distribution, whereas in pigmented lesions (as previously mentioned), the analysis of vascular structures provides secondary clues to the diagnosis.
criteria.notes: Reasoning rule rather than a scoring system: it sets how much weight an agent should place on level 5 and level 6 evidence for a given image.

criteria.name: two_step_algorithm_step_1
criteria.known_limitation: Basal cell carcinoma and melanoma can manifest overlapping features leading to some BCCs being classified as melanocytic and some melanomas as nonmelanocytic. Dermatofibroma displays a pigment network despite being nonmelanocytic.
criteria.source: Table 4, p444; p444 col 2; p446 col 1; Figure 7, p449
criteria.verbatim: The first step of the algorithm is based on a seven-level criterion ladder
criteria.notes: combination_logic is set to additive_score only because the vocabulary offers no term for an ordered ladder evaluated top-down; the ladder is not additive. Flagged as a vocabulary gap in Document 2.

gaps.issue: Source covers only one of the three entities merged into this label.
gaps.conflict: Lichen-planus-like keratosis is defined clinically by regression structures and peppering, which Table 5 lists as melanoma-specific (t_119, t_120, t_122). Without an explicit exception the graph will push these lesions toward mel. The document contains no such exception.

gaps.issue: Both entities appear only in the appendix vascular tables (pp D-E) and never in the Table 4 seven-level ladder. The class therefore has no step-1 route: an akiec lesion cannot be placed on the ladder at all, and only two evidence edges exist for it in the whole graph (strawberry pattern, glomerular vessels), both vascular and both dependent on the amelanotic weighting rule c_004.
gaps.conflict: The source gives no benign/malignant status for actinic keratosis. It is precancerous, and the document does not say so. Any agent reasoning from this graph alone has no basis for placing actinic keratosis on the benign/malignant axis, and Figure 7's terminal verdicts (nevus / suspect / malignant) offer no slot for it. Do not patch this from outside knowledge.

gaps.issue: Source covers cherry hemangioma and angiokeratoma but says nothing about pyogenic granuloma or hemorrhage, which HAM10000 also merges into vasc.
gaps.conflict: Level 4 evidence is entirely lacunae-based. A hemorrhage or pyogenic granuloma showing no lacunae has no positive route to vasc in this graph and will fall through to level 7 (structureless) or be argued toward mel via milky-red globules (t_263).

gaps.issue: Dermatofibroma appears only in the Table 4 footnote * and in the Figure 7 branch list. It has exactly two positive evidence edges in the whole document (peripheral delicate pigment network, central scar-like area), and its only ladder relationship is an exception rather than a level of its own.
gaps.conflict: The one additional clue the source offers for dermatofibroma is palpation-based (a firm lesion that dimples inward), which is not recoverable from an image and was excluded per instruction. df is therefore the thinnest-supported class in the graph after akiec.

gaps.issue: The nine benign patterns of Figure 3 are the only positive evidence base for nv, and the source supplies names without definitions (definition_absent_in_source: true on t_140 through t_148). A vision model cannot be told what 'patchy reticular' or 'two components' means from this document.
gaps.conflict: Reported, not filled: no definitions were invented for these patterns.
